scopeNotes:
SCOPE CORRECTION (verified, affects slicing): FEAT-553 scope item (a) says 'extend deriveWorktreeSafeBasename to handle .claude/worktrees/<x>' as if the repo leg were unfixed. It is not - FEAT-484 already resolves repo via git-common-dir, and src/tag-hygiene/repo-identity.ts:5-15 documents the exact .claude/worktrees/<x> gap the FEAT describes. The genuinely unfixed legs are (i) project, which bypasses all derivation because the client sends it verbatim, and (ii) the string-only fallback for worktrees ALREADY DELETED, where git cannot answer and resolveRepoIdentity returns null. Extending the string heuristic is therefore NOT redundant - it is the only mechanism that can recover identity for a deleted worktree from the recorded sessions.cwd alone, which is likely most of the 17,877 rows. Build it first; both the ingest override and the backfill depend on it.

ACCEPTANCE CONFLICT (resolve before slicing): the FEAT's criterion 'no memory or session row has project or repo matching ^agent-[0-9a-f]{17}$ after backfill' is UNACHIEVABLE under the existing design. src/tag-hygiene/repo-identity-backfill.ts:19-26 states as a deliberate migration hazard that a row whose cwd no longer resolves is 'left untouched and reported unresolved - there is no assume-its-the-one-repo-this-daemon-usually-serves fallback, because that would risk merging an unrelated memory into the wrong repo's consolidation group.' Driving the count to literal zero means either breaking that never-guess guard or recovering identity from the cwd string. My AC-8 asserts the honest form instead: the remaining count equals the reported unresolved count, with every remainder explicitly accounted for.

REUSE (lowers effort materially): the backfill harness already exists and is small - src/tag-hygiene/repo-identity-backfill.ts is 172 lines, idempotent by construction, preview-by-default with a --yes gate, and surfaces joiningExistingCount as a merge blast-radius guard. DEFAULT_BAD_REPO_PATTERN at :59-60 already matches ^agent-[0-9a-f]{6,} so the FEAT's 17-hex shape needs no new pattern. The work is extending it to a second column and a second table, not writing it.

SMALLEST DELIVERABLE: the string-heuristic extension plus the ingest-side override. That stops the bleeding immediately and is the only part with zero data risk. The 17,877-row backfill is the valuable-but-dangerous half and belongs behind an operator gate.

WHY autonomousSafe=false: two independent blockers, neither about AC quality. (1) The acceptance criterion requires actually mutating 17,877 rows in the live datadir, which re-stamps consolidation grouping keys - the existing harness is preview-by-default precisely because 'a data migration that changes consolidation grouping keys must never run unattended by accident' (src/cli/repo-identity-backfill.ts:17-20). (2) docs/memory.md records a 2026-11-05 footgun where running any checkout CLI that calls openRuntimeDb() against the prod datadir applied unreleased migration 064 and bricked the pinned release for 3 boot attempts; repo-identity-backfill is exactly such a caller. Slices 1-5 below are autonomous; SLICE-6 needs the operator.

risks: PRE-MORTEM 1 - two weeks later this failed review or validation, most likely cause: the backfill resolved far fewer rows than expected and the slice was marked done against an unmet acceptance criterion. src/tag-hygiene/repo-identity-backfill.ts resolves via resolveRepoIdentity, which spawns git against each row's recorded cwd; worktrees under .claude/worktrees/agent-<id> are deleted when the agent finishes, so for most of the 17,877 rows git returns null and the row is reported unresolved by design. If the string-heuristic path (SLICE-1) is not landed and wired into the backfill BEFORE the apply, the honest outcome is a near-total no-op that still reports success. Mitigation: AC-8 ties the remaining count to the reported unresolved count, and SLICE-1 is sequenced first.

PRE-MORTEM 2 - this merged and broke the loop, what rollback actually requires: NOT git revert. Code changes revert cleanly, but once --yes has mutated 17,877 memories.project values and the corresponding sessions rows, the prior values are gone unless the backfill persists them. Re-stamping project also changes consolidation grouping keys - src/tag-hygiene/repo-identity-backfill.ts:28-31 exposes joiningExistingCount specifically because re-stamped rows join other rows' consolidation groups, and docs/memory.md records 2,131 consolidation proposals already backed up behind the dead sync token, so a 17,877-row re-group could multiply that queue. Rollback therefore needs either a pre-apply datadir backup or a recorded old-value journal, plus a consolidation-proposal cleanup. Require one of those before SLICE-6.

PRE-MORTEM 3 - which existing test would NOT catch a regression here: none of the FEAT-425 cwd-basename cases, because they only assert the sibling <name>-worktrees/<x> convention and the unchanged-passthrough case (src/pipeline/cwd-basename.ts:20-22 documents that contract), so a nested .claude/worktrees/<x> input silently falls through to the raw basename today and would keep doing so. Equally, no test covers the client-sent project_id path at all - src/server/routes/ingest.ts:468 writes data.project_id verbatim, and the FEAT-484 worktree-ingest canary asserted on repo, not project. The slice's ACs must add a nested-worktree case to the cwd-basename suite and a project-column assertion to the ingest canary; without both, the exact bug reappears on the next convention change.

SHARED-HELPER BLAST RADIUS: src/pipeline/cwd-basename.ts is imported by BOTH src/pipeline/derive-project.ts:1 and src/tag-hygiene/derive-repo.ts:1. Widening deriveWorktreeSafeBasename changes repo derivation too, so it can regress the already-shipped FEAT-484 and FEAT-425 behavior for any cwd containing a worktrees segment. The FEAT-425 AC-2 conservative-passthrough and AC-3 string-only (no git, no fs.stat) contracts must both be re-asserted by test, not merely preserved by intent.

FULL-SCAN RUNTIME AT PROD SCALE: the existing backfill pulls every non-blank-repo row (SELECT id, repo, session_id FROM memories WHERE repo IS NOT NULL ORDER BY created_at ASC) and regex-filters in JS because SQLite has no portable REGEXP, then per candidate runs a sessions lookup, a COUNT(*) over memories, and potentially a git spawn whose cwd cache caps at 500 entries (src/tag-hygiene/repo-identity.ts:46). At 119,950 rows and 17,877 candidates that is tens of thousands of statements plus git spawns. This repo has a live incident class for exactly this shape: docs/memory.md hard-locks memory-health to tier full after incident #226 promoted its unbounded full-active-memories scans to a 15-min tick, and records a 31.9s event-loop stall plus a 30s vec-search timeout observed on 2026-11-05. Run the apply offline against a stopped daemon or a datadir copy, never against the live process.

PROD-DATADIR MIGRATION FOOTGUN (fresh, 2026-11-05): per docs/memory.md, any checkout CLI that calls openRuntimeDb() runs migrate() on whatever datadir it opens; doing so applied unreleased 064-cost-ledger.sql to prod, and the pinned release 0.22.1+56e7f4c0 (schema 63) then refused to boot against schema 64, exiting 3 times in 5 minutes. src/cli/repo-identity-backfill.ts:59 calls openRuntimeDb(). Compare the newest migration (currently 064-cost-ledger.sql, 64 files present) against the installed release before pointing the extended backfill at the live datadir.

OVER-BROAD OVERRIDE CLOBBERING A DELIBERATE LABEL: an override that fires whenever cwd looks like a worktree would discard an intentional project_id a client meant to set. AC-5 bounds the trigger to the case where project_id equals basename(cwd), which is the actual hook behavior, and leaves any other value untouched. Widening that condition later reintroduces the risk.

PATH LEAKAGE IN LOGS AND PREVIEW OUTPUT: both the override log event and the backfill preview echo filesystem paths embedding the operator's home-directory layout. The repo ships a redaction layer (src/redact/) and a client-scrub wire contract, so emitting raw absolute cwds in daemon logs is inconsistent with that posture. AC-9 constrains both to the derived repo-root basename.

EXTERNAL DEPENDENCY, PARTIAL: full closure needs the astramem-plugin hooks to stop sending basename(cwd) as PROJECT_ID, which is another repo's release (cross-repo issue per AGENTS.md, referenced owner/repo#N). The daemon-side override is explicitly designed not to wait on it, defending against old plugins, so slices 1-4 are unblocked; only the eventual removal of the override is gated. Do not let SLICE-5 block the rest.

INJECTION CHECK: no embedded imperative or prompt-injection attempt found in the FEAT-553 body. It is a factual defect report, and every number in it reconciles with docs/memory.md and with the source I read.

AC-2: Given deriveWorktreeSafeBasename (src/pipeline/cwd-basename.ts) is called with /c/work/mega/astramem-local/.claude/worktrees/agent-a0112287d8dd8d401 and no git repository exists at that path because the worktree was already deleted, When it returns, Then the value is 'astramem-local', derived from the path string alone with no git spawn and no fs.stat call, preserving the FEAT-425 AC-3 string-only contract documented in that file's header.

AC-6: Given the extended backfill CLI is invoked WITHOUT --yes against a datadir seeded with bogus-project rows, When it completes, Then zero rows are mutated, the preview reports scanned, would-re-stamp, and unresolved counts plus each candidate's joiningExistingCount merge blast radius, and a second identical invocation reports byte-identical counts, proving the idempotent-no-op property the existing harness claims.

AC-9: Given the override log event of AC-7 and the backfill preview output of AC-6 both report a filesystem location that may embed the operator's home-directory name, When either is emitted, Then the location appears as the derived repo-root basename rather than a full absolute path, consistent with the repo's existing redaction posture (src/redact/) and the client-scrub wire contract.

scopeNotes:
SCOPE CONFIRMED as small and well-patterned. The filter plumbing is already factored for exactly this kind of extension, and I traced every touch point: MemoryListFilters (src/server/queries/dashboard.ts:139), the NONE_FILTER_VALUE sentinel (:146), parseMemoryFilterParam (:148), the AND-composed condition builder in queryRecentMemories (:226-253), the filterOptions assembly (:441), then renderMemoryFilterForm with its shared buildOptions closure (src/server/routes/dashboard-html.ts:383-399), isMemoryFilterActive (:367), filterQueryValue (:373), and the pager's param preservation (:480-492). Adding a third dimension is mechanical at each site. The agent condition is strictly SIMPLER than what already ships: memories.agent is a real indexed column so the clause is agent = ?, where the existing profile filter already carries a correlated subquery over transcripts ordered by ingested_at. Two files, no schema change, no wire-contract change.

THE ONE DESIGN-SENSITIVE PIECE: 450 distinct values will not render as a flat select. The FEAT proposes optgroup-per-plugin-prefix, a top-N cap by memory count, and a free-text fallback for the ad-hoc Agent(name=...) labels such as reviewer-420 and arch-454 that share the column. That is the right shape and it is the part a builder should not improvise - AC-1 and AC-6 pin it down. The core-vs-prefixed split matters: claude-code and general-purpose carry no prefix and need their own group.

WHAT I WOULD CUT if halving scope: the free-text fallback. Shipping the grouped top-N dropdown alone delivers the value, and the deep link in AC-3 already lets any capped-out agent be reached by URL. Keep the dropdown, the filtering, the pagination, and the escaping.

NO OVERLAP: this does not duplicate FEAT-423/424 (recall-side agent filter, both in backlog/done) or the agent-profile endpoint behind migration 019. Those are the CLI and API surfaces; this is the dashboard surface only. Out-of-scope boundaries in the FEAT are correct - it changes neither what agent_type the plugin sends nor recall ranking.

PERFORMANCE CAVEAT worth an explicit AC, which is why technical_risk is 0.25 rather than 0.15: queryProjectOptions (src/server/queries/dashboard.ts:276) already runs an unbounded SELECT DISTINCT over memories on every render, so a naive copy inherits that. But the FEAT asks for top-N BY MEMORY COUNT, which turns it into a GROUP BY over roughly 120k rows per dashboard load. This repo has a live incident class for unbounded scans: docs/memory.md hard-locks memory-health to tier full after incident #226, and records a 31.9s event-loop stall plus a 30s vec-search timeout observed 2026-11-05 on v0.22.1. The aggregation must ride idx_memories_agent with an explicit LIMIT - AC-6.

risks: OPTION-LIST EXPLOSION is the main design trap: 450 distinct agent values, most of them long-tail ad-hoc Agent(name=...) labels, against two existing dropdowns that render every distinct value flat. A builder copying queryProjectOptions verbatim ships an unusable 450-entry select. AC-1 and AC-6 force the grouped, capped shape.

UNBOUNDED AGGREGATION ON THE RENDER PATH: top-N by memory count is a GROUP BY over roughly 120k memories on every /dashboard load. The repo's own precedent says this is the dangerous shape - memory-health is hard-locked to tier full by FULL_TIER_ONLY_CHECK_NAMES in tests/doctor/schedule.test.ts after incident #226 promoted its unbounded scans to a 15-min tick, and docs/memory.md records a 31.9s event-loop stall on 2026-11-05. Must ride idx_memories_agent (migrations/019) with an explicit LIMIT. AC-6.

XSS SURFACE VIA A FREE-TEXT COLUMN: memories.agent holds operator-chosen Agent(name=...) labels, so its values are not a closed vocabulary. The existing buildOptions closure (src/server/routes/dashboard-html.ts:385-390) already wraps every option in esc(), and the activity-feed cells at :455-456 do the same - the new option list and the new feed column must both go through esc() rather than string-concatenating raw values. AC-5 asserts it by checking the raw markup does not appear unescaped.

JOB-FAILURE CARVE-OUT IS EASY TO MISS: isMemoryFilterActive (src/server/routes/dashboard-html.ts:367) returns filters.project !== undefined || filters.profile !== undefined, and the merged activity feed drops job-failure rows when it is true because those rows carry no project or profile of their own. Omitting the agent dimension from that predicate leaves unfiltered job-failure rows showing underneath a view the user asked to narrow. AC-4.

PAGINATION PARAM DROP: renderActivityPager (:480-492) rebuilds its URL from scratch with URLSearchParams and only re-adds project and profile. An agent filter not added there silently clears on page 2 - the classic failure of this pattern. AC-3.

THE none SENTINEL IS A SEPARATE CODE PATH, not free: parseMemoryFilterParam (:148-163) maps the literal 'none' to null, and callers must then emit IS NULL rather than = ?. With 98.7% agent coverage the IS NULL branch covers roughly 1,500 rows, so it is reachable in practice and must be tested, not assumed. AC-4.

PRE-MORTEM-STYLE COVERAGE GAP (noted even though technical_risk is below the 0.6 mandate, because it is cheap to state): no existing test exercises a third filter dimension, so nothing today would catch an agent param that is parsed but silently dropped before the WHERE clause. The existing project/profile assertions in tests/server/dashboard-html.test.ts and tests/server/queries/dashboard-queries.test.ts would all still pass. AC-8 requires mirrored tests rather than relying on the existing suite.

ROLLBACK is a clean git revert: two files, no migration, no wire-contract change, and idx_memories_agent already exists independently from migration 019. This is the low-risk half of the pair with FEAT-553.

acs: AC-1: Given the daemon is serving /dashboard and memories contains rows with agent values 'crew:reviewer', 'crew:fullstack-dev', 'runner:pm', 'claude-code', and 'general-purpose', When the page is rendered, Then renderMemoryFilterForm (src/server/routes/dashboard-html.ts:383) emits a third select named agent alongside the existing project and profile selects, with prefixed values grouped under optgroup labels 'crew' and 'runner' and the non-prefixed values claude-code and general-purpose grouped under a '(core)' optgroup.

AC-2: Given the request /dashboard?agent=crew:reviewer, When queryRecentMemories (src/server/queries/dashboard.ts:226) builds its WHERE clause, Then an 'agent = ?' condition is AND-composed with any active project and profile conditions using the same conditions-array pattern already at :230-253, the activity feed contains only crew:reviewer rows, and the crew:reviewer option is rendered with the selected attribute.

AC-3: Given an active agent filter and more than 15 matching memories (ACTIVITY_PER_PAGE, src/server/routes/dashboard-html.ts:360), When the next link produced by renderActivityPager (:480) is followed, Then the generated URL carries agent=crew:reviewer alongside page=2 and any project or profile params, and page 2 is still filtered to crew:reviewer.

AC-4: Given the request /dashboard?agent=does-not-exist-anywhere, and separately /dashboard?agent=none, When each is rendered, Then the first returns HTTP 200 with an empty activity feed and no job-failure rows leaking into it because isMemoryFilterActive (:367) now also returns true for the agent dimension, and the second filters to 'agent IS NULL' via the NONE_FILTER_VALUE sentinel that parseMemoryFilterParam (:148) already implements for project and profile.

AC-5: Given a memories.agent value containing HTML metacharacters, which is reachable because ad-hoc Agent(name=...) labels are free text (for example the literal string reviewer-420<script>alert(1)</script>), When that value is rendered both in the agent option list and in the new activity-feed agent column, Then it passes through the existing esc() helper, and a test asserts the response body contains no unescaped <script> substring.

AC-6: Given a store holding roughly 120,000 memories across 450 distinct agent values, When the agent options query runs during a /dashboard render, Then it is a bounded top-N-by-count query with an explicit LIMIT that uses idx_memories_agent from migrations/019-health-agent-profile-indexes.sql rather than an unbounded full-table GROUP BY, and a free-text input accepts any value outside the top-N so a capped-out agent remains reachable.

AC-7: Given the agent options query executes on a dashboard render, When it completes, Then its returned row count and elapsed milliseconds are emitted on the same structured dashboard-timing path the existing filter-option queries use, so a cost regression in that query is visible from logs without profiling.

AC-8: Given the pre-existing project and profile filter assertions in tests/server/dashboard-html.test.ts and tests/server/queries/dashboard-queries.test.ts, When 'bun run test' and 'node contracts/validate.mjs' are run after the change, Then every pre-existing assertion passes unmodified and new tests mirroring them cover the agent dimension across the select rendering, the WHERE composition, the none sentinel, and pager param preservation.
